cells.tense: You're the one deciding how this gets built, and you're keeping the people with you warm while you do it.
cells.ask: let yourself picture what comes after this holds, and start building toward that too.
cells.core:
You're the one deciding how this gets built, and you're keeping the people with you warm while you do it. This is what tending looks like when it's going well — you set a shape people can actually work inside, you know how much to pour in and when to stop, and the momentum you've made holds without you pushing it. What you've made is real, and it's carrying people.

That steadiness isn't just maintenance. It's earned enough to dream forward. Let yourself picture what comes after this holds, and start building toward that too — the structure can carry more than it's carrying, and the warmth you've kept going is exactly what makes the next thing possible.
cells.sheetLine: You set the shape and keep everyone moving with you, and you can afford to build past it now.
cells.verb: keeping the fire that keeps everyone moving
cells.place: where the shape of things gets decided and set

cells.tense: You're holding everything up before it's asked for, bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: check what's actually true right now before you fix what isn't broken yet.
cells.core:
Keeping a structure alive and warm is steady work, and when it's going well you're the one who decides what holds and who moves with it. Right now you're doing that ahead of time — holding everything up before it's asked for, bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived. Every loose end gets tightened the moment you spot it, and the structure that was supposed to give people room to move has started to feel like something they have to get through.

Tending this hard ahead of time burns the fire you're trying to keep. Check what's actually true right now before you fix what isn't broken yet — clarity about what's really in front of you does more than another round of preemptive securing.

cells.tense: You're standing at the edge of shaping something and you haven't stepped over, and you're still back at that edge.
cells.ask: end one thing that's already finished so new ground opens up.
cells.core:
Shaping how things get built is steady, warm work, and when you're in it you set a container people can move inside without being managed. Right now you're at the edge of it, not in it — the structures you'd set are still sitting unbuilt, and you're not stepping forward into that. The capacity hasn't gone; the arriving hasn't happened. You're still standing where you stopped.

Getting yourself to move isn't the way back — trying harder at a seat that's already quiet just drains it further. End one thing that's already finished so new ground opens up. Set down what's over, and the energy for what comes next has somewhere to go.

cells.tense: The choices are already being made and they're being made through you, but you're calling it the work or the moment.
cells.ask: say plainly that you set one of the things you've been crediting to circumstance.
cells.core:
You already shape how things get organized here — you decide what structure makes sense, you set the pace, you're the one people look to when the shape of a thing is unclear. That's the capacity doing its real work: keeping something moving and warm, deciding what the frame will be. It's already happening in how you move through the day.

What hasn't happened is you claiming that shaping as yours. Say plainly that you set one of the things you've been crediting to circumstance — not as a boast, just as the truth of where it came from. Then it's yours to work with on purpose, and the warmth that keeps people moving stops being something that happens to you.
